questions.text: Which is a recommended Wi-Fi security option when supported?
questions.explanation: WPA3 is a modern Wi-Fi security option.

options: Systematically identifying and resolving a problem
questions.explanation: Troubleshooting is a structured process for narrowing down causes.

questions.text: What does HTTPS generally help protect?
options: Data exchanged with a website in transit
questions.explanation: HTTPS encrypts web traffic in transit but does not guarantee a site is trustworthy.

questions.text: Why compare a second device on the same Wi-Fi network?
options: To determine whether the issue is device-specific or network-wide
questions.explanation: Comparison helps determine the likely scope of the fault.

questions.text: Why is a strong Wi-Fi password useful?
options: It reduces unauthorized access to the wireless network
questions.explanation: Strong authentication helps restrict access to trusted users.

questions.text: Why is a padlock icon not enough to prove a site is legitimate?
options: HTTPS encrypts the connection but scammers can also use HTTPS
All HTTPS sites are government sites
questions.explanation: Encryption and website legitimacy are different security questions.

questions.text: A learner finds two similar Wi-Fi names in a cafe. What should they do?
options: Choose the one with the most suspicious login page
Ask staff to verify the official network before connecting
Share their password to test it
questions.explanation: Verify the network name to reduce the risk of an impersonating hotspot.

questions.text: Only one laptop cannot connect but all other devices can. What should be checked first?
options: The internet service for the entire country
The laptop's Wi-Fi status, selected network, and saved settings
questions.explanation: Begin by investigating the single affected device.

questions.text: A learner receives a browser warning about an invalid certificate. What is safest?
options: Do not bypass the warning for sensitive activity; verify the site and connection
Assume the warning is always a joke
questions.explanation: Certificate errors require verification, especially before sharing sensitive information.

questions.text: All devices lose internet but can still print locally. What is the best initial diagnosis?
options: Local LAN works; examine gateway or internet service
Every device has the same virus
Wi-Fi passwords must all be wrong
questions.explanation: Local function plus widespread internet failure points upstream.

questions.text: A router restart does not restore access and the provider reports an outage. What should users do?
options: Record the outage and use a trusted alternative if needed
questions.explanation: An external service outage is not corrected by random local configuration changes.

questions.text: Which troubleshooting strategy produces the clearest evidence?
options: Change passwords, DNS, router, and cables simultaneously
Skip checking whether all devices are affected
Assume the first guess is correct
Test one variable at a time and note outcomes
questions.explanation: Controlled checks help isolate causes and avoid introducing new faults.
